summary: Southern Idaho TPA lookout near McCall: a 1937 two-story log house, replaced by a duplicate in 1963, staffed in fire season and drive-up.

facts.design: two-story D-6 cabin, essentially a small house with two floors; 1963 duplicate of the 1937 building

access.note: Drive-up site on Southern Idaho TPA land. NHLR says it welcomes visitors. No source reports a closure.

events.note: Fire-detection site since the 1920s, first as a camp, per NHLR
Planned station announced in the Idaho Statesman, to be installed the next spring about 15 miles southwest of McCall
Two-story 20x20 log structure erected with Civilian Conservation Corps labor
Fire under a quarter acre southeast of the lookout, controlled by four smokejumpers; cause not stated
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, October 3, 2020

corrections.why: The 1963 date is the replacement. The first two-story structure was built in 1937 with CCC labor.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1936 Idaho Statesman item placed the planned station about 15 miles southwest of McCall. Keeping Watch now places the lookout about eleven miles from McCall. The story gives both.
The NHLR describes a log structure and the 1937 newspaper says log. firelookout.com says log and frame. The story reports both descriptions.

notes_for_editor: The brief's built year of 1963 is the replacement; the original two-story house is dated 1937. Elevation differs by source (NHLR 7,334 ft; firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts about 7,350 ft) but elevation is not a facts key here. Current staffing dates are undated on every source. A Facebook search snippet (not read, not used) mentions a seasonal closure notice for No Business, worth checking before publication. Access is set to public from NHLR's welcome statement and the drive-up listing.
